## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

In #40066, empty CPU lists were filtered out via `if cpus` in `get_cpu_ids_by_node()`. However, after per-rank thread/NUMA core binding (e.g., running with `TP=6`), `get_cpu_ids_by_node()` only returns the CPUs within the current rank's bound NUMA node, reducing `n_numa_node` from the total number of NUMA nodes (e.g., 6) to `1`.

Meanwhile, `get_free_cpu_memory()` queries the **system-wide (or cgroup-constrained) available memory** via `psutil.virtual_memory().available` and `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.*`, rather than the available memory of the bound NUMA node. Dividing the global free memory by `n_numa_node = 1` instead of total NUMA nodes significantly overestimates the per-rank KV cache memory budget, while actual memory allocation remains strictly restricted by NUMA binding, leading to OOM errors (e.g., when running Grok-2 with TP=6).

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->
Cache get_cpu_ids_by_node results to ensure consistent NUMA node detection across binders.

nodes.body:
@xinguozhu-2026 Does it work if we add `@lru_cache(maxsize=1)` to `get_cpu_ids_by_node`? Every binder calls it to pick its CPUs before binding, so the cached result always reflects the affinity before the thread/NUMA binding (`6` NUMA nodes in the case that you're fixing).
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/132b0f0ae73aa8cf812b72e9b98c89d1a3e1ac85/python/sglang/srt/utils/common.py#L4512

> @xinguozhu-2026 Does it work if we add `@lru_cache(maxsize=1)` to `get_cpu_ids_by_node`? Every binder calls it to pick its CPUs before binding, so the cached result always reflects the affinity before the thread/NUMA binding (`6` NUMA nodes in the case that you're fixing).
> 
> https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/132b0f0ae73aa8cf812b72e9b98c89d1a3e1ac85/python/sglang/srt/utils/common.py#L4512

yes, it works, this should fix the NUMA node issue. However, there's still one corner case:

``` bash
numactl --cpunodebind=2,3 --membind=2,3 \
  <...run_server_args...> \
  --tp-size 2
```

In this case, it would still overestimate the memory budget for each rank, potentially leading to OOM. 
If we consider this scenario out of scope, adding the cache should be fine.

> > @xinguozhu-2026 Does it work if we add `@lru_cache(maxsize=1)` to `get_cpu_ids_by_node`? Every binder calls it to pick its CPUs before binding, so the cached result always reflects the affinity before the thread/NUMA binding (`6` NUMA nodes in the case that you're fixing).
> > https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/132b0f0ae73aa8cf812b72e9b98c89d1a3e1ac85/python/sglang/srt/utils/common.py#L4512
> 
> yes, it works, this should fix the NUMA node issue. However, there's still one corner case:
> 
> ```shell
> numactl --cpunodebind=2,3 --membind=2,3 \
>   <...run_server_args...> \
>   --tp-size 2
> ```
> 
> In this case, it would still overestimate the memory budget for each rank, potentially leading to OOM. If we consider this scenario out of scope, adding the cache should be fine.

For the regression of https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40066 itself, the current fix should be good. For the case you mentioned, I'd suggest submit a follow-up PR to address it separately.
This assumes all local ranks share the same memory cgroup. If some belong to separate cgroups, the divisor is too large, underestimating the per-rank cgroup allowance.

@@ -907,6 +905,36 @@ def get_free_cpu_memory() -> int:
     return free_cpu_memory
 
 
+def get_free_cpu_memory_per_rank() -> float:
+    free_cpu_memory = psutil.virtual_memory().available
+
+    numa_count = len({node for _, _, _, node in parse_lscpu_topology()}) or 1
+    memory_per_rank = free_cpu_memory / numa_count
+
+    instance_max_cpu_memory = get_instance_memory_status("/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max")
+    instance_current_cpu_memory = get_instance_memory_status(
+        "/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.current"
+    )
+    if instance_max_cpu_memory is not None and instance_current_cpu_memory is not None:
+        instance_free_cpu_memory = max(
+            0, instance_max_cpu_memory - instance_current_cpu_memory
+        )
+        # Assume local workers share one cgroup; independent DP replicas have
+        # separate WORLD groups, so include them in the allowance split.
+        num_local_ranks = (
+            torch.distributed.get_world_size()
+            * get_parallel().dp_size
+            // get_parallel().nnodes
+            if torch.distributed.is_initialized()
+            else 1
+        )
